solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get frustrated as former partner repeats a failing

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: failing letters have collapsed out of their proper order, so the words repeats and a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone loses patience because an ex keeps making the same mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' alone is the definition, in the sense 'that really gets me'; 'frustrated as' only links it to the wordplay. 'failing' rearranges REPEATS A into ASPERATE, which follows EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone is colloquially to annoy or irritate them, which is exactly what exasperating them means.

clue.text: Imitate speech opposing covers

indicators.note: the words speech opposing cover, or contain, the letters sought, which run across the two words

explanation.surface: A debater mimics the rival's speech while arguing against what it covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' is the hiding signal: the letters sit across the end of 'speech' and the start of 'opposing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat back what someone has said or done is to imitate it, as a mimic or parrot does.

clue.text: One flying player gets through instead of 100

indicators.note: instead of says one piece takes the place of another inside the word for player

parts.note: an actor is a player on the stage
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
via means by way of, or through

explanation.surface: A flying member of a team breaks through in place of a centurion, or some such sports report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instead of' swaps C (Roman 100) in ACTOR for VIA, giving A-VIA-TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot of an aircraft is someone who flies, the noun for whoever is at the controls.

clue.text: Rework my rap with clean-cut singer

indicators.note: to rework something is to remake it, so the letters of my rap and clean-cut are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A rapper revamps a track with a wholesome-looking crooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rework' rearranges the thirteen letters of MY RAP and CLEAN-CUT into the singer's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles' bassist and songwriter is among the best-known singers in pop history, an example of the category.

clue.text: Grass about flesh that's exposed

indicators.note: about says the grass goes round the flesh, enclosing it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of marshes
veal is calf flesh eaten as meat

explanation.surface: An informer talks about some bare skin that's on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like an informer but supplies REED, which goes 'about' VEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid bare or uncovered has been disclosed, made visible to all.

clue.text: Doctrine that's the same from Northern and Southern viewpoints

definitions.note: a principle held as true, a belief or dogma; the word for it is a palindrome, so it alone is the wordplay too

indicators.text: the same from Northern and Southern viewpoints
indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the top (north) or the bottom (south) gives the same letters, so the word is a palindrome

parts.note: a principle held as true, a belief or dogma; the word for it is a palindrome, so it alone is the wordplay too

explanation.surface: A principle that looks identical whether viewed from the north or the south of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, Northern and Southern mean top and bottom: the word reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, which is what a doctrine is.

clue.text: Tired defeat

definitions.meaning: to overcome or win against an opponent

explanation.surface: Exhausted after a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an informal adjective meaning exhausted and a verb meaning to overcome a rival.

clue.text: Knit one of a pair given to 5 topped and tailed

indicators.note: given to says the twin is handed over into the trimmed word, going inside it
topping and tailing removes the first and last letters of the 5 answer

parts.note: the answer to 5 down, the doctrine
a twin is one of a pair born together

explanation.surface: A knitting instruction: work one stitch of a pair onto the fifth, trimming the ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' trims TENET to ENE; TWIN goes in after its first two letters, EN-TWIN-E.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit things together is to twist or interweave them, joining them closely.

clue.text: Offer head warmth

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as a resignation or payment
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Offer a hand of warmth to someone, a kindly gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is the geographic sense: NESS, a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbours Dungeness or Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection and warm feeling towards someone is a kind of warmth of heart.

clue.text: Island nation reflected after chap discovered Japanese writing

indicators.note: after says the reversed letters come after the chap's middle
discovered means with its covers removed, so the outer letters of chap go
reflected means turned back as in a mirror, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A man stripped bare discovers a Japanese text about an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' reverses the island and nation pair to give IKU; 'discovered' strips CHAP to HA, which the reversal comes 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: The haiku is a short Japanese verse form of three lines, a form of Japanese writing.

clue.text: Game for better wine, drunkenly get barrel

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests staggering out of order, so the letters of get are rearranged

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: A gambler improves a wine by downing a barrel of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' scrambles GET to GTE between VIN and TUN. 'better' is one who bets, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon's French-named original is a card game played for stakes, so a gambler's game.

clue.text: More passionate about English supporting ship in rubbish novel

indicators.note: in a down light, the supporting part sits underneath, so it comes second
in puts the ship inside the rubbish

parts.note: tat is shoddy goods, rubbish
the ark is Noah's ship

indicators.note: about says the more passionate word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: hotter means more heated, more ardent

explanation.surface: A tale of hot-blooded English people backing a ship in a dreadful novel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'supporting' means below: H-E-OTTER sits under T-ARK-AT. 'novel' is the definition, not part of 'rubbish novel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Williamson's 1927 book about an otter's life in Devon is a famous English novel.

clue.text: Often in TT?

parts.note: the letters TT show one T after another, and T is short for time; often is the plain meaning

explanation.surface: How frequently something happens at the TT, the Isle of Man motorbike races.
explanation.walkthrough: TT suggests the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races, but read as letters it is T (time) after T (time).
explanation.definitionFit: Repeatedly, on many occasions, is what frequently, or often, means.

clue.text: Average signal — on this?

parts.note: medium means middling, average
to wave is to signal with the hand

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which band an ordinary broadcast signal travels on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: an average signal might be broadcast on this radio band.
explanation.definitionFit: The AM radio band between long and short wavelengths carries ordinary broadcast signals, a middle-range band.

clue.text: Improved journalist employs Republican during recess

indicators.note: employs here means takes in, so the journalist holds the rest

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

indicators.note: during says the Republican comes within the recess

parts.note: a niche is a recess in a wall

explanation.surface: An improved reporter hires a Republican while Congress is on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' looks like a parliamentary break but is NICHE; R goes in 'during' it, and ED 'employs' the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made richer or better in quality, as enriched soil or food, has been improved.

clue.text: Beware sailors in underground place

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, old school slang
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: A warning about sailors lurking somewhere below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (Latin 'beware') was the lookout's warning in British public-school slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cave beneath the surface is a subterranean chamber, an underground place.

clue.text: Democrat enters debates about support for person retiring

indicators.note: enters says the Democrat goes inside the rearranged letters
about here means round and round, all over the place, so the word debates is rearranged

parts.note: the letters of debates, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Democrat joins debates about backing a politician who is standing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DEBATES to BESTEAD, which D 'enters'. 'retiring' means going to bed, not leaving office.
explanation.definitionFit: The frame of a bed holds up the sleeper, so it supports someone who has gone to bed.

clue.text: Pass on the setter's role

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so the setter's (setter is) gives I'M
a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler hands over their job to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the setter's' is short for 'the setter is', giving I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on knowledge or news is to convey or communicate it.

clue.text: Have gangs set upon son?

indicators.note: in a down light the gangs are set upon, on top of, the son

parts.note: posses are bands of men, gangs

explanation.surface: A question whether gangs have attacked someone's son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set upon' looks like attack, but in a down light it puts POSSES above S.
explanation.definitionFit: To own or hold something is to have it.

clue.text: Dad's here, freaking out people with loud shocks?

indicators.note: freaking out means going wild, so the letters of dad's here are rearranged

explanation.surface: Father turns up and panics people who are startled by noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freaking out' rearranges DAD'S HERE. 'shocks' are masses of hair, and 'loud' means garish, not noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocks are thick masses of hair; people with vivid ginger hair have showy, loud ones.

clue.text: Road ran around state

indicators.note: around suggests moving about, so the letters of road ran are rearranged

explanation.surface: A road ran around the edges of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges ROAD RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenean principality is a small independent country, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Playing modern studios is ill-judged

indicators.note: playing with letters means moving them about, so modern studios is rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic says that music performed in contemporary studios is a poor choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges MODERN STUDIOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wrongly judged or misread by others has been misjudged, not properly understood.

clue.text: Swelling fame delays turning up in part

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Celebrity holds things up, puffing someone up a little.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'turning up' reads the letters hidden in 'fame delays' from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedema is the medical term for swelling caused by fluid in body tissues.

clue.text: Old German won hearts

parts.note: to win something is to get it, so won gives got
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: An elderly German man won people's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goths were an ancient Germanic people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were an early Germanic people, so one of them is an old German.

clue.text: Expert emptied tray with inadequate-sounding fuel for torch

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: emptied removes the contents, leaving only the outer letters of tray
sounding says the letters entered match the spoken form of the word for inadequate

parts.note: lean means meagre, thin, inadequate

explanation.surface: A skilled worker empties a tray of meagre fuel for a blowtorch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' leaves TY from TRAY; 'sounding' turns LEAN into LENE, which is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: The gas burned with oxygen in welding torches is a classic fuel for a cutting flame.

clue.text: Landlord, not husband, returns carrying gold trunk

indicators.note: carrying says the reversed letters hold gold within them
returns says the remaining letters run backwards
not says the husband is taken away from the landlord

parts.note: a host keeps an inn, a landlord
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A landlord, single now, comes back with a trunk full of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops H from HOST, 'returns' reverses OST to TSO, and that is 'carrying' OR: T-OR-SO.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the main part of the body without head or limbs.

clue.text: Criminal hit with this point could become atheist

indicators.note: criminal signals an unlawful scramble: hit with the letters sought can be reordered into atheist

explanation.surface: A villain hits someone so hard at this spot that they might lose their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix 'hit' with the answer and you could make ATHEIST, so the answer is ATHEIST less HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four compass points, so a point of direction.

clue.text: Black tree died, and another — that's rubbish

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
the alder is a tree
another tree, the ash

explanation.surface: A dead black tree and another one beside it are written off as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and another' means a second tree after ALDER: ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Senseless talk or writing, nonsense, is rubbish in the figurative sense.
